Description Title: Repeated Behavior Score Drops Over an Extended Period Despite Positive Match History Hello Dota 2 Team, I am reporting a recurring issue with my Behavior Score and Communication Score that has been frustrating me for a long time. This is not an isolated incident. For an extended period, I have repeatedly experienced the same pattern: my scores increase after playing matches, but when the next 15-match summary is updated, they drop again. This cycle has happened multiple times, making it extremely difficult for me to maintain a score above the 3000 threshold required to access ranked matchmaking. After my latest 15 matches, my Behavior Score dropped from 3058 to 2953, a decrease of 105 points. My latest match summary shows: - 13 positive matches out of 15 - 29 Commends received - 0 abandoned matches - 0 Communication Reports - Excessive Reports: No - 2 reported matches I consistently try to play fairly and positively, often receive MVP awards, and receive numerous Commends. Despite this, my scores repeatedly fluctuate, and I keep losing access to ranked matchmaking. I understand that Commends and positive matches do not guarantee an increase in Behavior Score. However, the repeated nature of these drops over an extended period makes me concerned that there may be an issue with the scoring system or how my account's scores are being calculated. Could you please investigate this recurring issue or clarify what could be causing these repeated decreases? I can provide screenshots of my previous scores, updated scores, and match summaries as evidence. Thank you for your time and consideration. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots Description Hello Valve Development Team, I would like to report a possible issue with Dota 2's reporting and Behavior Score system. My Behavior Score recently dropped from 5,926 to 5,461, a loss of 465 points, and I received a temporary matchmaking restriction of approximately four hours. My latest Conduct Summary Matches evaluated: 15 Positive matches: 12 Reported matches: 3 Reports: 9 Reporting parties: 9 Communication reports: 0 Abandoned matches: 0 Commends: 21 Excessive Reports: Yes Description of the problem My account currently has communication restrictions due to its Behavior Score, meaning I cannot use text or voice chat. When teammates become toxic, I mute them, report inappropriate behavior when necessary, and continue playing normally. I use map pings to communicate gameplay information. Sometimes teammates repeatedly demand that I join fights that I believe are strategically unfavorable. When I choose not to participate in those fights to avoid unnecessary deaths, I suspect some teammates retaliate by reporting me. I understand that refusing a teammate's call does not automatically prove that their report is abusive. However, I am concerned that the reporting system may be penalizing legitimate strategic disagreements. Expected behavior Reports should be evaluated based on actual disruptive gameplay rather than simply disagreement between teammates. Actual behavior My account received nine reports across three reported matches, followed by a significant Behavior Score reduction and an approximately four-hour matchmaking restriction. I cannot confirm that these reports directly caused the restriction, but the timing raises concerns. Request Could the development team investigate whether the reporting system is correctly handling potentially retaliatory reports? If a system error is identified, I respectfully request that the resulting Behavior Score reduction and matchmaking restriction be reviewed and corrected where possible. Thank you for your time and consideration. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No Description Dear Valve Support Team / Dota 2 Developers, I am writing to report a serious matchmaking bug in Dota 2 that is causing unfair penalties on my account, even though I am not refusing or abandoning any matches. Today, October 18, 2026, I experienced the following issue: 1. I queued for a Dota 2 match normally and waited for the matchmaking system to find a game. 2. However, **the "ACCEPT MATCH" window never appeared on my screen**, making it completely impossible for me to accept the match. 3. Despite never receiving the option to accept, the system incorrectly treated the situation as a failure to ready up. 4. As a result, I received an unfair **30-minute matchmaking penalty**. 5. I am concerned that this bug will continue happening and cause increasingly longer penalties. At this point, I do not even know when I will be able to play normally again without being unfairly punished. **This is not a player-related issue.** I am actively trying to play Dota 2, but the matchmaking system is failing to display the match acceptance window. I cannot accept a match when the game does not give me the opportunity to do so. I respectfully request: - An investigation into this matchmaking bug and the failure of the "ACCEPT MATCH" window to appear. - Removal of the unfair matchmaking penalties caused by this technical issue. - Correction of any negative impact on my Behavior Score or Conduct Summary. - A solution to prevent this issue from happening again and causing even longer matchmaking bans. **I should not be penalized for failing to accept a match when the acceptance window never appeared in the first place.** I sincerely hope this issue can be investigated and resolved as soon as possible, as it is preventing me from enjoying the game normally. Today, October 18, 2026, I experienced the following server issue: 1. I queued for a match normally and clicked "ACCEPT" as soon as it appeared. 2. Instead of loading into hero selection, the client kicked me back to the main menu. 3. I immediately attempted to click the "Reconnect" button multiple times, but the server failed to respond and refused the connection due to a server outage/collapse. 4. As a result, I received a 24-hour matchmaking penalty ("Matching disabled due to excessive reports, failing to ready-up, abandoning or other negative behavior"). This is not a player issue. I actively tried to enter and reconnect to the match, but server instability prevented me from connecting. I respectfully request: - An investigation into this server connection drop to prevent further unfair penalties for affected players. - Removal or correction of any negative impact on my Behavior Score or Conduct Summary caused by this server outage. I should not be penalized for a server crash that was completely beyond my control. At the same time, my Behavior Score dropped from 2,215 to 1,465. Recently, I have been playing Turbo matches to practice Invoker. I deliberately chose Turbo because I am still learning the hero and do not want to negatively affect other players in ranked or regular All Pick matches. I have not intentionally fed, griefed, or attempted to ruin anyone's games. I have simply been practicing a difficult hero while trying my best to win. I understand that making mistakes while learning a hero is normal, but I do not believe that poor performance alone should be treated as intentional griefing. Description Please add an optional matchmaking setting that allows players to specify the **minimum Behavior Quality** they are willing to accept. Dota Plus already evaluates the Behavior Quality of a match before the player accepts it. However, there is currently no way to tell the matchmaker to continue searching when the predicted behavior quality is below the player's preference. ## Current Problem A matchmaking search can take **5-10 minutes**. When a match is finally found, it may show **Disruptive** behavior. If the player doesn't want to accept that match, the current process becomes: > **Queue -> wait 5-10 minutes -> Disruptive Behavior -> decline -> queue again** This can repeat several times. In my experience, roughly **4 out of 5 matches found** can have Disruptive Behavior. The frustrating part is that the matchmaking system already knows the Behavior Quality before presenting the match. Instead of requiring the player to manually decline and restart the search, it should be possible to tell the matchmaker to continue searching automatically. ## Suggested Solution Add a matchmaking preference such as: **Minimum Behavior Quality:** - Any - Acceptable or better - Good or better - Very Good For example: > **Minimum Behavior Quality: Good or better** > > ⚠️ Higher behavior requirements may significantly increase matchmaking time. If I select **Good or better**, the matchmaker should simply continue searching when it finds a lobby below that threshold instead of presenting it to me. I am completely fine with a longer queue. I would rather wait **30-40 minutes continuously** for a suitable match than repeatedly wait 5-10 minutes, decline a Disruptive Behavior match, and restart the queue. ## Optional Setting - No Impact on Players Who Want Faster Queues This should be entirely optional. The default could remain: > **Minimum Behavior Quality: Any** Players who prioritize queue speed would experience no change. Players who care more about Behavior Quality could voluntarily accept longer matchmaking times. ## Why This Would Help - Eliminates repeated manual declining and requeueing. - Gives players more control over the tradeoff between **queue time and Behavior Quality**. - Makes maintaining a high Behavior Score more meaningful. - Gives players with poor behavior an additional incentive to improve. - Does not negatively affect players who prefer faster matchmaking because the filter would be optional. The Dota 2 behavior score system appears to have a systemic issue in low-behavior brackets: reports seem to carry disproportionate weight compared to commends. For players whose communication is already muted, this creates a loop where playing well and winning leads to enemy reports, which keeps the behavior score low and prevents recovery. Environment Game: Dota 2 Platform: Steam, PC Account ID: unsoftiz Steam ID: unsoftiz Behavior score: ~1500 (now) , ~2500 (before) Duration: ~1-2 years Communication status: muted by system Winrate over period: 50-60%+ Matches played trying to recover: about 500-800+ Steps to reproduce Have a low behavior score (~1500) and muted communication. Play ranked matches and perform well (win lane, carry, high winrate). Win games or lose close games. Observe reports from enemy team (when winning) and teammates (when losing). Check behavior score after multiple games with commends. Expected behavior Commends should offset reports enough to allow recovery. Reports should be validated or weighted based on context. Muted players should not be punished for chat they cannot use. Playing well and winning should not trigger a net negative behavior score. Actual behavior Behavior score remains low or decreases. Reports appear to have near-100% success rate in low-behavior brackets. Commends do not seem to offset even a single report. Creates an endless loop: low score → reports weighted heavily → low score. Impact Dedicated players who want to play competitively are locked out of ranked matchmaking for years. The system was designed to punish toxic behavior, but it appears to punish performance and winning in low-behavior pools. Additional context I have spent thousands of hours and around $150 on this account. I want to grind to Immortal, but the behavior algorithm has blocked ranked matchmaking. I can provide match IDs, behavior score history, and screenshots for review. Request Please have the Dota team investigate how automated reports are weighted in low-behavior brackets, especially for players with muted communication and high winrates. If this is not the correct GitHub repo, please point me to the official issue tracker. If you need more information (match IDs, screenshots, etc.), let me know. Thanks. These are gameplay reports from lost games. - Almost the entire 3,949-point drop comes from four large penalties of roughly −700 to −1,000 each. ## The matches **Match 9008909843 (Sep 20) — Wraith King, 3/6/9, lost.** Three of my teammates were in one party (Spirit Breaker, Lina, Templar Assassin). I was still convicted and sent to Low Priority, the second time that same day. **Match 9012524823 (Sep 23) — Wraith King, 7/15/7, lost.** Yes, I died a lot. But I also had the second-highest hero damage (25.1k) and the highest tower damage (1.9k) on my team. Losing a lane is not a crime. 4. **Party stacks have too much power against solo players.** A group that is losing can easily push a solo player into Overwatch. 5. **It is a death spiral.** The lower my score, the worse my teammates, the more often games collapse, the more reports I get, the lower my score. A clean game gives about 10–13 points. That means one conviction erases 80–100 clean games. I cannot enjoy a game where I have to play not to win, but to avoid making anyone upset after a loss. That is not Dota anymore. The joy is completely gone. ## About money Over the years I have regularly spent money on Dota 2. I supported the game because I believed in it. As of today, that is over. I will not spend anything more on Dota 2 while the behavior system works like this. ## What I am asking for 1. **A real appeal process** for Overwatch convictions, with a human review on request. 2. **Transparency:** tell the player which match they were convicted for and which behavior was the reason. 3. **A clear line between "bad game" and "griefing".** Deaths alone, or losing a lane, should not be enough for a conviction. 4. **Full context for Overwatch reviewers**, not a short fragment of the match. 5. **Accountability for reviewers** who vote "guilty" on almost every case without real review. 6. **Less weight for reports from party stacks against solo players**, and the Avoid Party protection in all modes. 7. **Proportional recovery**, so one bad week does not take hundreds of hours to fix. 8. If possible, please review my account and my recent convictions. I am writing this not just for myself, but because I see many players with exactly the same story. Please fix this system. I understand that Dota 2 needs a system to deal with toxic behavior and reports. However, I believe the current system is unfair in my situation and creates a cycle that makes it extremely difficult to improve my Behavior Score. I have played my matches respectfully and have always tried to win. I do not intentionally insult, harass or disrespect other players. In fact, I currently cannot even use chat properly, so I have very limited ability to communicate with other players in the first place. This creates a serious problem: if another player asks me something or expects communication from me, I may not be able to respond. I can then still receive reports because I did not communicate, even though the reason I did not communicate is that the system itself restricts my ability to do so. There is also a problem when playing with a group. Communication is restricted in the lobby, even in situations where players are simply trying to coordinate before or around a match. This makes it even harder to communicate normally and demonstrate positive behavior. Another issue is that players can receive reports simply because a game was lost or because teammates blame a particular player, such as the carry. Losing a match does not automatically mean that a player behaved badly or intentionally played poorly. A report system should distinguish between actual toxic behavior and normal gameplay disagreements, mistakes, or losing a match. Most importantly, I currently feel trapped in a cycle: * My Behavior Score is low. * Because of the low score, my communication is restricted. * I can't communicate in the lobby with my party in certain situations, including when we are trying to coordinate around the lobby. I also believe that if a player is prevented from participating in a paid feature because of their Behavior Score, there should be a clear warning before the purchase is made. I purchased the Battle Cup Ticket, but I am now unable to use it. Please review my account and my Behavior Score history, including the reports and communication restrictions applied to my account. I would also like you to consider whether the current restrictions are preventing me from improving the very score that is causing those restrictions. I would appreciate a concrete solution rather than simply being told to "increase my Behavior Score", because under the current restrictions I do not see a realistic way to do that. Thank you. Description Hello. I have been playing Dota 2 for a long time, and I am writing not to dispute a ban or complain about a specific match. I want to draw attention to a problem in the Communication Score and report system that, in my view, harms the game and punishes innocent players. I agree that Behavior Score is a working and necessary thing. It genuinely restrains those who ruin games: AFK players, feeders, people who intentionally spoil the match. But Communication Score works differently, and here is the fundamental problem. Dota 2 is a team game where communication is critical. When a player is forcibly deprived of the ability to write and speak, it is not only he who suffers, but also his four teammates. You cannot call missing, you cannot warn about a gank, you cannot call for Roshan, you cannot coordinate a push. So the punishment of one person turns into a punishment for the entire team. At the same time, the game already has a mute button. Any player can mute any teammate or opponent and no longer see or hear them. It turns out that the forced silence system duplicates a function that every player already has, but does it for everyone at once, without their consent. A separate problem is the mechanism of reports for communication itself. It does not analyze what exactly a person wrote or said. A report triggers based on the number of complaints. Because of this, a "communication report" easily turns into a tool of revenge: a person can be reported for bad play, for an incomprehensible move, for disagreeing with someone's decision- and he will receive a silence, even though he insulted no one. This has been discussed in the community for a long time, including by well-known players and streamers. Dendi publicly said that the report system "just doesn't work"; Stray228 compared forced mute in a team game to a situation where a footballer is left on the field but forbidden to pass. So on paper, the idea of separating "behavior" and "communication" looks logical. The problem is in the execution: the system triggers too easily on false complaints and gives a normal player almost no opportunity to prove that he did nothing wrong. What, in my opinion, should be changed: 1)Remove the forced global mute, or at least make it "off by default," so that teammates can decide for themselves whether to hear this player or not. 2)Make it so that a communication report triggers only with real analysis of text or voice, and not based on the number of complaints. 3)Leave players under silence with basic pings and the chat wheel- they are not toxicity and are needed for the game. 4)Return reports to their original meaning: to punish for ruining the game, not for an "unpleasant manner of communication." I understand that this is not a technical support issue, but I ask you to forward this to the Dota 2 team. Thank you for the game and for actually reading feedback. Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I am reporting a problem with the current Overwatch and behavior restriction system and, more specifically, the lack of transparency or an appeal/review mechanism for players who receive an Overwatch conviction. I have been playing Dota 2 since November 4, 2012, and this account has been part of my gaming history for almost 14 years. Recently, my Behavior Score dropped from 7,987 to 3,077 in a relatively short period of time. During this period I received multiple Low Priority penalties, and my communication features were eventually disabled. The most recent penalty was particularly concerning because it was issued after an Overwatch review. The match in question is: Match ID: 9001535070 Hero: Outworld Destroyer Result: Victory Score: 23 / 4 / 15 MVP Reports: 2 Commends: 28 After contacting Steam Support, I specifically asked them to investigate what happened to my account or, if Steam Support could not investigate Overwatch decisions, to provide me with a way to contact the team responsible for reviewing them. Steam Support confirmed that the matchmaking restriction was caused by an Overwatch conviction and later confirmed that the conviction was based on this exact match (9001535070). However, Steam Support also told me that: - they do not review or remove Overwatch restrictions; - they cannot provide contact information for the Overwatch team; - and there is no alternative appeal channel they can provide. I understand that Steam Support may not have the ability to manually remove an Overwatch restriction. I am not asking for special treatment or for Valve to simply remove my penalty because I disagree with it. My concern is the lack of transparency. If an Overwatch conviction is based on a specific match, I believe the affected player should at least be able to understand what behavior was considered a violation. At the moment, I have no information about: 1. What specific behavior in match 9001535070 resulted in the conviction. 2. What category of violation was identified. 3. What part or timestamp of the replay was considered evidence. 4. Whether the conviction was reviewed by multiple reviewers or how the verdict was validated. 5. Whether there is any mechanism to challenge an incorrect Overwatch verdict. I fully understand that a good KDA, winning a match, or receiving MVP does not automatically prove that no violation occurred. I am therefore not claiming that my statistics alone prove the conviction was wrong. The problem is that I have no way to determine what I supposedly did wrong in the first place. This is especially concerning because the affected player cannot meaningfully learn from or challenge a decision when the only information provided is that an Overwatch conviction occurred. There is also an important context regarding my recent Behavior Score history. Between two of my recent conduct summaries, my Behavior Score changed from 3,902 to 3,077. During those seven matches I won 6 out of 7 games. The final match in that sequence was the Outworld Destroyer game mentioned above, which was a 23/4/15 victory with 28 commends and 2 reports. Again, I am not presenting this as proof that the Overwatch verdict must be wrong. I am providing it because the circumstances make it particularly important for me to understand what behavior was actually reviewed and why it resulted in a conviction. I am also a long-time Dota 2 streamer and content creator. Because I regularly stream my games, I have experienced situations where viewers or other players intentionally watch the stream and interact with the game around it. I cannot prove that this caused the reports or the Overwatch conviction, so I am not presenting it as a fact. However, I believe it is a relevant possibility when investigating unusual reporting patterns on a streaming account. I am not asking Valve to reveal the identities of Overwatch reviewers or any private information about them. I am asking for a reasonable way for an affected player to understand and, when appropriate, challenge an Overwatch decision. My questions to the Dota 2 team are therefore: - Is there currently any way for a player to obtain information about the specific violation that resulted in an Overwatch conviction? - Is there any mechanism for reviewing or appealing a potentially incorrect Overwatch verdict? - How does Valve ensure that Overwatch convictions are sufficiently validated before they result in matchmaking restrictions and major Behavior Score penalties? - If a conviction is found to be incorrect, is there any mechanism to correct the resulting Behavior Score or other penalties? I have been playing Dota 2 for almost 14 years and I genuinely do not want to leave the game because of a punishment that I cannot understand or challenge. I would appreciate it if the Dota 2 team could clarify how this system is intended to work from the perspective of the player receiving the conviction. Description ### Description I encountered a VAC-related issue that prevented me from reconnecting to an ongoing ranked match after Dota 2 crashed. Some time ago, I accidentally deleted the normal Dota 2 desktop shortcut created by Steam. Instead of recreating the standard Steam shortcut, I manually added a shortcut by browsing to the Dota 2 executable and placing that shortcut on my desktop. On September 17, 2026, I launched Dota 2 through this manually created desktop shortcut. Everything initially worked normally: - Steam was running. - Dota 2 launched normally. - I was able to search for a public ranked match. - VAC did not display any warning before matchmaking. - I connected to the match and played normally. Near the end of the match, when the game was already close to being won, Dota 2 crashed after Alt+Tab. I immediately relaunched Dota 2 and attempted to reconnect to the same match. At this point, I received the following message: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device. If you do not resolve this issue, online play may be unavailable." Because of this VAC verification error, I could not reconnect to the ongoing match. I tried: - Restarting Dota 2 several times. - Restarting Steam. - Restarting my PC. - Checking my Windows security configuration. My system security configuration was: - Windows 11 64-bit - Secure Boot: Enabled - TPM version: 2.0 The issue was finally resolved when I stopped launching Dota 2 through the manually created shortcut and instead launched Dota 2 directly from my Steam Library. After launching the exact same Dota 2 installation from the Steam Library, VAC verification worked normally again. No changes were made to Windows, BIOS, TPM, Secure Boot, game files or hardware between the failed VAC verification and the successful launch from the Steam Library. ### Why this appears to be a bug The important part is that Dota 2 / VAC allowed me to: 1. Launch the game using this shortcut. 2. Enter matchmaking. 3. Accept a ranked match. 4. Connect to a VAC-secured server. 5. Play almost the entire match normally. However, after the client crashed, the same launch method caused VAC to reject the device and prevented me from reconnecting to the match. If launching Dota 2 directly through this type of shortcut is not considered valid by VAC, I believe the game should detect this before the player is allowed to enter matchmaking. Allowing the player to enter a ranked match normally and then preventing them from reconnecting after a client crash can cause an unavoidable abandon and ranked / behavior penalties. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Delete or do not use the standard Dota 2 Steam desktop shortcut. 2. Manually create a desktop shortcut by browsing to the Dota 2 executable. 3. Make sure Steam is running. 4. Launch Dota 2 using the manually created shortcut. 5. Search for and enter an online matchmaking game. 6. During the match, close or crash Dota 2. 7. Relaunch Dota 2 using the same manually created shortcut. 8. Attempt to reconnect to the match. 9. VAC may display: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device." 10. Close Dota 2. 11. Launch Dota 2 directly from the Steam Library. 12. VAC verification works normally again. ### Expected behavior If Dota 2 allows a player to enter a VAC-secured ranked match, restarting the client during that match should not cause VAC to reject the same device solely because the game was launched through a different shortcut. Alternatively, if this method of launching Dota 2 is unsupported, the player should be warned or prevented from entering matchmaking before the match starts. ### Match information Match ID: 9003543610 Date: September 17, 2026 ### Additional software / system information Overwolf is installed on my PC and I use it for Path of Exile 2. Overwolf and its associated applications were completely closed while I was playing Dota 2 and when this VAC error occurred. I am including this only as additional system information and I am not claiming that Overwolf caused the issue. Secure Boot: Enabled TPM: 2.0 OS: Windows 11 64-bit ### Penalty / Match review request Because this issue occurred during an active ranked match and directly prevented me from reconnecting, I would appreciate it if the affected match could also be reviewed. I did not intentionally abandon the match. I attempted to reconnect immediately and repeatedly, including restarting the game and my PC. If an abandon, MMR loss, Behavior Score / Conduct Score reduction, matchmaking restriction, Low Priority penalty or any other automated penalty was applied specifically because I could not reconnect due to this VAC verification issue, please consider reversing or excluding that penalty if technically possible. Match ID: 9003543610 ### Attachments I have a screenshot of the VAC error showing: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device." I can also provide additional Steam System Information or system diagnostics if required. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots Support (Ari) directed me to post this here because the current Behavior Score system has a fundamental design flaw at the ~3k level. The way the communication ban interacts with automated reports creates an impossible, inescapable loop for players who are genuinely trying to win and improve their score. **The Core Design Flaw: Playing with Bots** Communication is the absolute core of any multiplayer team game. When you completely remove a player's ability to communicate, you turn a team-based strategic game into a single-player experience. I might as well be playing against bots, because the interaction with my team is exactly the same. When you drop below 6,000 behavior score, you cannot ask for help, coordinate with your team, ping the map effectively, or explain macro decisions. Because you cannot explain your actions, teammates lacking map awareness automatically assume you are griefing, report you, and the automated system issues severe punishments with zero human oversight. **Case Study from a Recent Match:** To demonstrate how this algorithm fails, here is exactly what happened in my recent match. I played Axe offlane with a Phoenix support against a very tough Spectre and Enchantress lane. Phoenix was role-abusing, taking farm and last hits instead of helping me survive. From a gameplay design perspective, what is the intended correct play here? - **Option A:** Stand at a safe distance on the lane, get zero gold, and leech experience from my support (who can safely solo the lane due to range and escape skills). This is widely considered griefing. - **Option B:** Leave the unplayable lane, move to the jungle to recover, and let the support have the lane. I chose Option B. I stopped contesting Phoenix for farm and went to jungle. Because I was completely muted by the system, I couldn't tell my team why I was doing this. Here is how the situation escalated: - Phoenix followed me to the jungle to steal last hits from a triple-stacked camp I made. - He/she then moved to the safe lane to stand in trees, doing nothing, but to leech XP from our carries. - He/she went in to bushes to AFK for about 15 seconds from a middle of teamfight with full hp. I ended up doing the supports (Phoenix) work, buying 3 Observers and 6 Sentries, while the actual support bought exactly 2 Sentries in a 42-minute game. I also made several immediate buybacks after dying. Again, because I was muted, I couldn't explain that this was a deliberate macro strategy. Returning to the lane meant instant death from Spectre and Enchantress. Buying back allowed me to farm safer areas and stay close to the game's overall XP progression. The scoreboard at the end of the game proves this strategy worked: I successfully kept up with the level progression and was on the exact same level as everyone else. Once I got the relevant basic items (Vanguard, Blink Dagger to counter the 4 ranged enemies, and a Blade Mail), I rotated back, tanked damage, initiated fights, and we actually won the game. I was even commended by our carries. **The Automated Punishment & The Single Draft Trap:** Despite adapting to a griefing teammate, buying the wards, playing to the very end, and winning the game, the automated system immediately hit me with a 4-hour matchmaking ban, a -500 behavior score drop, and a Low Priority penalty requiring 3 Single Draft wins to escape. This Single Draft penalty is completely contradictory and feeds directly into the same broken loop: - You are forced to play with actual, legitimate griefers who are in Low Priority for the right reasons. - Because the hero pool is restricted, teammates frequently pick unsuitable heroes for the lineup, leading to setups with 4 or 5 hard carries. - People refuse to adapt their roles, or they simply have never played the random heroes they were given. - This inevitably leads to more griefing, ruined games, and consequently, more false reports from tilted teammates. - As a result, your behavior score continues to tank even further based on false reports while you are just trying to win your 3 mandatory matches. I am a 37-year-old man, and I do not believe I have ever been a toxic player. I do not throw rage fits, and I have never abandoned a match midway through unless there was a power outage (which hasn't happened in years). I am a team player—in non-role queue games, if everyone else picks a carry or a tank, I will always try to pick a support or whatever role the team is missing. To be completely honest, I do not even remember why my behavior score originally dropped to ~3000, because it happened several years ago. Since then, due to how this communication ban and punishment loop operates, it has been practically impossible to raise it back up. **The Mathematical Impossibility:** The most broken part of this system is the math behind recovering your score: - **The Grind:** If you manage to play 15 games without a single negative ping or false report, the system updates your score by about 250 points. That is roughly 12.5 hours of playing. - **The Punishment:** After this single match—where I didn't communicate at all, adapted to a bad lane, and won the game—I lost 500 points. - **The Result:** 25 hours of clean grinding wiped out by an automated algorithm in an instant. My score dropped back to 2,500. Now, on top of a 4-hour ban and the Single Draft prison, I am forced to play AT LEAST another 25 hours of unranked games just to unlock ranked matchmaking again, just for the exact same problem to repeat. **The "For Fun" Report Exploit:** The vulnerability of this automated system is public knowledge. There are multiple YouTube videos right now showing players admitting they report others purely for fun. They proudly showcase their "Action Taken" lists on screen, openly acknowledging that none of the players they reported actually did anything wrong—yet your automated system still punishes those innocent players based on malicious reports. **Conclusion** I completely understand that a multiplayer game needs a punishment system to keep the community healthy, but this current implementation is absolutely not the right way to do it. How can a player improve their behavior score when the system mutes them from explaining legitimate gameplay decisions, forces them into an endless 25-hour grind for minimal points, traps them in Single Draft with actual griefers, and empowers those griefers to hand out automated bans? I have played Dota for 14 years, but I have completely lost faith in how this game and its automated systems are being managed. I used to absolutely hate League of Legends, but this complete lack of respect for your player base has forced me to reconsider. It has become glaringly obvious that Valve only values high-ranked and professional players, while us paying, casual players who actually fund the game are completely ignored. You are simply riding on the legend of the game at this point. This fundamentally broken system is undoubtedly driving many dedicated players to League of Legends, and I am now one of them. I will be canceling my long-term subscription upon making this transition. Description I want to raise a serious issue with the current Conduct Summary system. I recently lost around 1,200 Behavior/Communication Score after only a few incidents. I fed in one game, and I left another game due to circumstances that were not under my control. As a result, I received an enormous penalty that has effectively made normal communication and matchmaking extremely difficult for me. I understand that intentional feeding and abandoning games should have consequences. I am not asking Valve to remove penalties for genuinely bad behavior. The problem is the scale and lack of transparency of the punishment. One or two incidents can apparently result in a massive loss of Conduct Score, while the player has no meaningful way to understand exactly how the penalty was calculated or appeal an incorrect punishment. Dota 2 is a team game. Communication is an important part of the experience, yet the current system can leave a player with what feels like a permanent muzzle simply because of a few bad games. I would strongly encourage Valve to consider: Making Conduct Score penalties proportional to the severity and frequency of actual offenses. Providing a clear explanation of why a player's score changed. Giving players a way to appeal obvious false or unfair reports. Preventing coordinated or abusive reporting from disproportionately affecting a player's score. Considering a player's long-term behavior instead of heavily weighting a small number of recent games. Making the Conduct Summary algorithm more transparent. I genuinely enjoy playing Dota 2, but when a single bad game or an unavoidable disconnect can cost an enormous amount of Conduct Score, it becomes incredibly frustrating. Please reconsider how aggressively the current system punishes isolated incidents. I am not asking for a system with no consequences. I am asking for a system that is transparent, proportional, and actually gives players a reasonable opportunity to recover from mistakes. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ Description **Request to rework or remove the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2** Hello Valve, I would like to ask you to seriously reconsider the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2. The problem is that a system designed to reduce toxicity has started to negatively affect one of the most important parts of Dota 2 - communication between teammates. Dota 2 is a team game. Players need to communicate constantly: call missing heroes, suggest objectives, coordinate Roshan, smokes, buybacks, item timings, team fights, lane swaps, defensive actions and dozens of other situations. However, the current system creates an environment where players are increasingly afraid to communicate at all. Players avoid using voice chat, text chat and sometimes even pings because any active interaction with teammates can potentially result in reports and a reduction of Communication Score. As a result, the safest way to protect your account and Behavior Score is simply to remain silent. This creates an absurd situation: **The optimal behavior in a competitive 5v5 team game is to avoid communicating with your team.** The consequences are clearly visible in matchmaking: * players rarely use voice chat; * important information is not communicated; * teammates do not discuss strategy; * players are afraid to criticize even obvious gameplay mistakes; * communication often starts only when the match is already lost; * coordinated play in solo matchmaking becomes significantly harder; * reports can effectively be used as a punishment for disagreement rather than actual toxic behavior. There is also an important distinction between **toxicity** and **communication that another player simply does not like**. Insults, harassment, racism, threats and intentional spam should obviously be punishable. But saying things such as: "Don't fight without buyback." "Please stop farming and come Roshan." "We need BKB before the next fight." "Don't go high ground now." "Can you TP bottom?" should not create a risk for a player's ability to communicate in future matches simply because another player disagreed with the call and decided to report them. The current system incentivizes silence instead of healthy team communication. I believe Valve should either substantially redesign this system or remove the communication restrictions in their current form. Possible improvements could include: 1. Separate actual toxic behavior from ordinary gameplay communication and disagreements. 2. Reduce the influence of mass communication reports when there is no evidence of abusive behavior. 3. Make Communication Score penalties more transparent so players understand exactly what behavior resulted in a restriction. 4. Do not remove essential team communication tools from players unless there is clear evidence of serious or repeated abuse. 5. Introduce stronger protection against report abuse after lost matches. 6. Evaluate the content and context of communication instead of relying primarily on the number of reports. 7. Preserve essential strategic communication such as voice, pings and gameplay calls wherever possible. Dota 2 is one of the most complex competitive team games ever created. Communication should be encouraged, not treated as a potential risk to the player's account. A system intended to combat toxicity should punish toxic behavior. It should not make silence the safest strategy. Please consider reviewing the current Communication/Behavior system and its impact on actual teamwork in matchmaking. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No To increase the behavior score, a player must play standard matches. 2. Playing standard matches as a solo queue player naturally triggers false, subjective reports from toxic party stacks. 3. The automated system accepts these reports (even for communication abuse on a completely muted account), lowering the score even further. This is a technical system loop that cannot be resolved automatically. Description Title: Fantasy card "Score" doesn't match sum of displayed emblem stat values (Core & Support banners) Description: On my Fantasy banners (TI 2026), the emblem stat values shown on the card do not add up to the displayed final Score, and it's unclear from the UI how the total is actually calculated. Mid banner (single player, no pairing) calculates correctly — Score matches expectations there. The issue only shows up on Core and Support banners, which are same-team pairs. Example 1 — Core banner ("Satanic & Noticed"): Creep Score (240%): 13,012.92 Courier Kills (320%): 4,634.18 Deaths (120%): 3,360.24 Stuns (260%): 6,799.12 Kills (300%): 9,671.73 Sum of above: 37,478.19 Displayed Score: 28,129.35 Difference: 9,348.84 (unexplained) Example 2 — Support banner ("9Class & Dukalis"): Obs Wards Planted (240%): 10,951.20 Teamfight (150%): 6,842.29 Runes Grabbed (240%): 3,891.60 Stuns (150%): 2,159.73 Smokes Used (110%): 4,673.35 Sum of above: 28,518.17 Displayed Score: 20,028.69 Difference: 8,489.48 (unexplained) Mid banner: works as expected — no discrepancy observed there (single-player banner, not a pair). Expected behavior: Either the Score should equal the sum of the five displayed emblem values, or the card should clarify how pair-based averaging, the Deaths penalty formula, and any half-weight "solo" stats (e.g. Courier Kills, Obs Wards, First Blood — stats only one player of the pair can typically get) are factored into the final total. This info isn't shown anywhere on the card. Actual behavior: No visible math on the card explains the consistent gap between the sum of the five stats and the final Score — happening on both pair-based banners (Core and Support) I've checked, while the single-player Mid banner is fine. This makes it impossible for players to verify their own Fantasy pair scoring is correct, and suggests the discrepancy is specifically tied to the pair-averaging logic. Steps to reproduce: Open Fantasy → Group Stage/Main Event View Core or Support banner for a same-team pair Compare the sum of the 5 emblem values to the "Score" total at the bottom of the card Compare Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I enjoy Dota and play it whenever I have free time. However, for several years now, I have been stuck in what feels like a nightmare of this game, with a Behavior Score fluctuating between 0 and 5,000. Since I don't play Ranked, I don't have the option to avoid parties. As many players know, party players tend to report solo players, shifting the blame for their own poor performance onto the one player who isn't in their group. This happens very often. Currently, I can't even reach 3,000 Behavior Score. It feels like the system intentionally places me in matches right when I'm about to hit that mark, matching me with a full party of four players — which means four reports. This leads me straight into Overwatch. And Overwatch, as it stands, almost always returns a guilty verdict. There are discussions where people admit they click "Guilty" on every case without reviewing the replay at all. As a result, you lose 1,000 points from the verdict, and the reports also throw you into Low Priority games, where you continue to get reported endlessly. In total, you lose around 1,500 points, and you're back to 1,000 Behavior Score. The cycle repeats endlessly, and there is simply no way out of it in the current state of the system. I see many other players reporting similar issues on your GitHub. About two months ago, I finally became so frustrated that I took a break after receiving 4 Low Priority games. I returned recently for the event and noticed that matchmaking had been reworked — I hoped the Behavior Score system had received some attention as well. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case. I struggled through those Low Priority games, managed to play 4 All Pick matches, and then received another punishment from Overwatch. In all 4 of those games, I was the only solo player on my team. There were constant pings directed at me, insults, and likely reports as well. I played well in all of those matches, and there was absolutely no valid reason for a penalty. I realize that nobody is going to review these games, but to support my claim, here is the Match ID from which I received the punishment: 8956143152. By the way, in that same match, the Terrorblade player destroys his items at 48:18. But naturally, no one will report him because he is playing with his friends in a party and can do whatever he wants — they are just having fun. I believe there are several ways to improve this system and potentially bring back hundreds, or even thousands, of players who have left because of these issues. For example: 1. Introduce a "Behavior Score Reset Token" as a reward in one of the events, at least once a year — for instance, in the Quartero's Curios event at level 150. This token would be non-tradable, non-giftable, and usable only once per account, setting the Behavior Score to its maximum value. Ruiners would drop back down in just a few games anyway, so this wouldn't harm normal players in any way. 2. Extend the "Avoid Party" feature to unranked matches, just as it already exists in Ranked. This would at least partially prevent situations where a solo player receives 4 reports and ends up in Overwatch, leading to automatic Low Priority games. 3. Increase the accountability and quality standards for Overwatch reviewers. Currently, there is no penalty for reviewers who hand out "Guilty" verdicts without properly reviewing the evidence. Implementing a quality check or a verification mechanism for Overwatch cases would ensure that only genuine griefers are punished, and innocent players are not caught in a faulty automated loop. Description The current Communication/Behavior Score system and its automated in-game mutes are actively hurting the matchmaking experience. Dota 2 is a highly competitive, team-oriented game that requires constant communication. The problems with the current mute system are: 1. System Abuse: The automated mute system is easily abused. Players frequently use communication reports to punish teammates for bad gameplay (missed spells, lost lanes), rather than actual toxicity. 2. Collateral Damage: A globally muted player cannot coordinate with their team (calling missing, Roshan timings, smoke ganks). This essentially punishes the 4 other innocent players on the team who are now playing at a severe disadvantage. 3. Impossible to Recover: Once a player's communication score drops, it is incredibly difficult to raise it back up because they cannot communicate to be commended, creating a vicious cycle. Suggested changes to rework the system: - Replace the forced absolute mute with a "soft mute". By default, the player is muted, but teammates should have a clear button to manually UNMUTE them if they want to coordinate. - Do not restrict essential gameplay pings and basic chat wheel commands for muted players. - Rework the automated penalty system so that report volume alone doesn't trigger immediate, severe communication bans without actual text/voice chat analysis. Please reconsider how this system operates, as it currently causes more frustration than it prevents. 4. Encouraging Griefing: The sudden in-game mute often demoralizes the team and triggers griefing behavior. For instance, in a recent match, immediately after a player received a system mute mid-game, two other teammates simply gave up and stopped playing entirely. is a long-standing and very frustrating issue in Dota 2 related to the communication system and the Behavior Score system. When a player has a low behavior score, is in low priority, or is in a muted/punished chat pool (due to reports), the in-game chat becomes restricted or disabled. As a result, the /roll command (which generates a random number to resolve disputes) stops working in all modes, including normal non-role queue matches (All Pick without strict role assignment). What this leads to: Draft Chaos. When two players both want to play mid (or carry/offlane), they have no fair way to decide who gets the role. Double Mid Syndrome. Since /roll is unavailable, players just lock a second mid hero anyway, turning the game into a toxic mess from minute zero. Game Ruining. Instead of a civilized resolution, arguments escalate, players start flaming each other, and often intentionally feed or grief because the dispute is only resolved by "who picks faster". Inequality. This issue disproportionately affects players with low behavior scores — who are already in a bad spot. Instead of giving them tools to resolve conflicts peacefully (like rolling), the system takes that tool away, making matches even more unbearable and preventing them from recovering their score. The Core Problem: /roll is NOT a social chat message; it is a gameplay mechanic (a console/chat command) that returns a random integer. Muting chat or restricting communication should not affect gameplay commands, especially in non-role queue modes where /roll is the only civilized way to distribute roles. Proposed Solution: Make the /roll command available regardless of "Low Priority", "Muted", or "Low Behavior Score" status. Alternatively, add a "Roll" button directly to the hero selection UI that is always functional (similar to how it works in tournament/captain's mode drafts or custom lobbies). This is a critical quality-of-life improvement for the community that would significantly reduce toxicity and the number of ruined Dota 2 developers and community, I would like to ask for clarification regarding the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. My current scores are: Behavior Score: 12,000 / 12,000 (maximum) Communication Score: 5,800 / 12,000 I regularly play Dota 2 and I do not intentionally grief, feed, destroy my items, abandon matches, throw games, or smurf. In ranked games, I play the roles assigned to me by the matchmaking system and try to play for the win. I also support Dota 2 financially and enjoy the game, which is why I would like to understand how this system works and how it could potentially be improved. I recently checked my Steam Personal Game Data → Dota 2 → Account → Incoming Match Player Report. My recent data shows Communication Reports even during periods where I had no abandons or excessive reports. For example: August 11: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 3 Communication Reports from 2 reporting parties August 8: - 15 matches - 14 positive matches - 1 reported match - 0 abandons - 4 Communication Reports from 3 reporting parties August 6: - 15 matches - 11 positive matches - 4 reported matches - 0 abandons - 7 total reports - 4 Communication Reports from 4 reporting parties August 2: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 0 Communication Reports My main question is: How can a player have a maximum Behavior Score of 12,000/12,000 while having a Communication Score of only 5,800/12,000? I understand that these are separate systems and that Communication Reports can affect Communication Score. However, I am concerned about the possibility of unjustified or retaliatory reports. There is another situation that I believe is worth considering. In a five-player team, it is possible that three players are in the same party and know each other. If one of these players has a disagreement with me, the other two party members may potentially report me simply to support their friend, even if they did not personally witness any actual communication violation. In this situation, what could start as a disagreement between two players could potentially result in multiple reports against the same player simply because several players are grouped together. For example, instead of receiving one report from the player involved in the disagreement, I could potentially receive reports from all three members of the party because they want to support their friend. This raises an important question: Does the Communication Score system take party relationships or coordinated/retaliatory reporting into account? If multiple members of the same party report the same player, are these reports treated completely independently, or does the system recognize that they may be related to the same incident? I believe this is important because otherwise a single conflict between two players could potentially have a disproportionately large effect on another player's Communication Score. Players can report each other because of disagreements, frustration after losing a game, disagreements about gameplay decisions, or personal conflicts. Therefore, I would like to understand how the system prevents abuse of Communication Reports. I contacted Steam Support about this issue. They told me that the scores are automated and that Steam Support cannot manually adjust them. They also stated that they do not provide additional information about how the behavior scoring system is calculated. They recommended that I bring this issue to the Dota 2 community and development forums. So this is what I am doing. I am NOT asking for my Communication Score to be manually increased. I would simply like to understand whether the current system can incorrectly penalize a player because of unjustified, retaliatory, or potentially coordinated Communication Reports, and whether there are mechanisms that prevent players from abusing the reporting system. I would also like to raise another question regarding the recovery of Communication Score. Why does the Communication Score not have some form of regular recalibration or review period, for example once a year? Would it be possible to introduce an annual recalibration, review, or another mechanism that would give players who have demonstrated consistently good behavior over a long period of time a clearer way to recover their Communication Score? In my subjective opinion, there appears to be a significant imbalance between losing Communication Score and recovering it. It feels like a player can receive Communication Reports relatively easily and potentially lose Communication Score very quickly, while recovering that lost score through consistently good behavior appears to be much slower. Even if a player makes a serious effort to communicate politely and avoid violations over a long period of time, recovering from a low Communication Score can feel extremely difficult. In other words, the negative effect of reports can appear very quickly, while the positive effect of consistently good behavior takes much longer to become visible. I believe that a regular recalibration or another transparent recovery mechanism could make the system feel more fair. It would also give players a clearer motivation to improve their behavior because they would know that consistently good behavior over time can meaningfully restore their Communication Score. If there is no way for players to verify whether reports against them were legitimate, how can they know what behavior they need to change? I would appreciate any clarification from the Dota 2 developers or experienced players who understand how the current system works. I am not asking for special treatment for my account. I am asking whether the current system could be improved to make Communication Score more resistant to report abuse and to provide players with a reasonable path to recover from a low score through consistently good behavior. I have attached screenshots of my Personal Game Data as evidence. Thank you for taking the time to read this and consider the Description Title: Feedback / Suggestion: Behavior Score system needs real-time updating and better balance for isolated bad games Body: Hi Valve team, I’d like to share some feedback regarding the current Behavior & Communication Score system. Currently, receiving a summary every 15 games makes the system feel rigid and unfair. A player can play 14 great games, have 1 bad game (or get targeted by a toxic party/tilted teammates), and end up with a heavily penalized report or even low priority. One single bad match shouldn't outweigh two weeks of good behavior. Suggestions for improvement: Real-time updates (similar to modern mobile competitive games): Instead of waiting 15 games for a batch update, let every single match influence the score dynamically. Weighted Recency: Recent games should hold meaningful weight, but isolated incidents shouldn't drastically ruin an entire reporting period. Better Variance Protection: A single bad game out of 15 should be treated as an anomaly, not a trend. This change would make the system feel much more transparent, fair, and encouraging for players who are actively trying to maintain high behavior scores. Description Dear Valve, I would like to share my experience with the behavior score system because I genuinely feel something is not working correctly in my case. Over the last several days, my behavior score has continued to decrease even though I play alone, focus on winning, and do my best to help my team. I don't understand why this is happening. I currently cannot even use chat, so I have no way to be toxic through text or voice communication. Despite that, my behavior score dropped from around 5,000 to about 4,000, and I received a 24-hour matchmaking ban. After this ban expires, I will most likely be placed into Low Priority, even though I don't believe I've done anything to deserve it. The most frustrating part is that I'm not a smurf or someone trying to ruin matches. I'm actually a relatively new player who wants to improve at Dota 2. I spend time learning heroes, watching guides, and trying to become a better teammate and player. I queue for ranked matches completely solo. Very often I get teammates who intentionally grief, give up early, or are simply much less experienced. Even in those situations, I keep playing until the end and sometimes manage to carry the game and win anyway. I don't abandon matches, I don't intentionally feed, and I always try my best regardless of how difficult the game becomes. Because of this, it's very confusing to see my behavior score constantly going down. It feels like I am being punished for something I didn't do. If players are reporting me simply because they are angry after a match or because I played differently than they expected, I hope those reports are being reviewed fairly. I understand that the behavior system is important for keeping the community healthy, and I support that goal. However, I also hope there is a way to identify cases where legitimate players are incorrectly losing behavior score. I would sincerely appreciate it if someone could review my account and the reports against it. If there has been a mistake, I kindly ask if my behavior score could be restored. I truly enjoy Dota 2 and want to continue improving, climbing the ranked ladder, and being a positive member of the community. Thank you for taking the time to read my message, and thank you for continuing to support the game.
